ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and officers against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (Global Affairs Canada), UN Security Council Consolidated List, Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) watchlist, RCMP/PEPMO designations, and as a banking de-risking measure, OFAC SDN and EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions lists. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), including domestic and foreign PEPs as defined by FINTRAC Guidance 71, undergo enhanced due diligence and senior management approval. Transaction monitoring reflects PCMLTFA Part 1 record-keeping and verification rules and the federal beneficial ownership transparency enhancements under Bill C-42 (CBCA ISC reporting to Corporations Canada).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (ISED) — NUANS name search via an approved NUANS service provider; portal: https://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/ccmc-cdcc.nsf/eng/home
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: CBCA s. 10 requires the corporate name to be in English, French, or bilingual form using the Roman alphabet; foreign-language transliterations are permitted only where rendered in Roman characters; the name must end with an approved legal element: 'Limited', 'Ltée', 'Incorporated', 'Inc.', 'Corporation', 'Corp.' (CBCA s. 10(2)); names must not be confusing with existing registered names, marks, or federally incorporated entities (CBCA s. 12(1)); the NUANS report must be dated no more than 90 days before filing.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Misleading terms implying government agency, criminal activity, or deceptive business scope
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written rejection from the Director of Corporations Canada, the applicant: (1) requests the specific grounds in writing; (2) files a formal written reconsideration with Corporations Canada Name Services within 30 days of the refusal, attaching the original NUANS report, proposed amendments, evidence of prior use, and a legal memorandum on non-confusion pursuant to CBCA s. 12 and the confusion factors in s. 10; (3) if reconsideration is denied, a fresh NUANS report may be used for a new name request, or the applicant may file an application for judicial review to the Federal Court of Canada under s. 18.1 of the Federal Courts Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. F-7, within 30 days of the final administrative decision; (4) concurrently, trademark clearance via the Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO) records is recommended prior to filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the CBCA registered office only where the service address is a physical location in Canada capable of accepting service of process; a licensed registered-agent virtual office is accepted by Corporations Canada and most provinces. For a reverse-logistics and quality-grading operation, a physical Canadian warehouse or distribution facility is strongly recommended to substantiate commercial purpose, GST/HST nexus, payroll, and the place of effective management (POEM) test under the Income Tax Act; purely virtual substance materially increases the CRA audit risk and may disqualify treaty benefits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_to_Medium: quantified baseline risk of 18% per annum for a compliant operating entity with a third-party logistics warehouse in Canada; elevated to approximately 55% if the registered office is purely virtual with no Canadian fixed asset, inventory, or payroll, particularly where annual gross turnover exceeds the GST threshold (CAD 30,000) or the CRA POEM test may shift residency.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, S.C. 1985, c. C-44, Part I (Incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under the Canada Business Corporations Act; shares may be issued as nil or nominal value with no par value
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Board Resolution of the Proposed Corporation: WHEREAS it is desired to incorporate a business corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act to engage in cross-border reverse logistics and returned goods quality grading; RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation be adopted substantially in the form attached hereto, and that the incorporator be authorized to execute the same; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be established at [Insert Full Address], and that the directors be authorized to change the same as necessary; RESOLVED, that the following persons be appointed as the first directors of the Corporation: [Insert Names and Addresses]; RESOLVED, that the initial share capital be fixed at [Number] common shares without par value, and that the incorporator subscribe for all such shares; RESOLVED, that the Corporation's banking and accounting systems be established, and that the officers be authorized to open bank accounts and execute necessary documents post-incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Submit Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the prescribed form including corporate name, registered office address, names and addresses of directors, share structure, and objects of the corporation. Submit electronically through the Corporations Canada portal along with the filing fee and director consent forms. Ensure all documents are notarized if required by applicable provincial law.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, provide additional information or make necessary amendments within 30 days to address any deficiencies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No dedicated federal industrial licensing board; provincial business registrations apply

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated wastewater, VOCs, or waste handling emissions; standard environmental compliance for logistics operations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: General compliance with workplace safety standards; no specific fire safety or structural load certifications required for reverse logistics and grading activities

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC), Business Registration Online (BRO) at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax-businesses/industry-specific/business-number.html, and the CRA 'My Business Account' and 'Represent a Client' portals; the GST/HST regime is administered federally under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. E-15) with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administering customs documentation at the border.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in Canada must obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN), which serves as the statutory TIN for income tax, GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts. The BN is procured by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or by using the Business Registration Online service; a non-resident corporation must additionally file Form RC460 (Non-Resident Business Number and GST/HST Registration) and provide supporting documentation (foreign certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, power of attorney, and the name of the Canadian representative or agent). Non-resident registration may be completed electronically through BRO or by paper; the CRA assigns the BN immediately, and the GST/HST account (RT) can be opened in the same application. Where the foreign corporation will be a participant in a Canadian partnership or a branch operation, it must also consider Ontario Extra-Provincial Registration or equivalent provincial extra-provincial licensing; a valid BN is a precondition for claiming input tax credits (ITCs) and for filing GST/HST returns electronically.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not maintain a US-style check-the-box regime; a Business Corporation (Inc. or Corp.) is automatically taxed at the entity level under Part I of the Income Tax Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. 1, 5th Supp.). Relevant elections and mechanisms include: (i) the s. 216 election for non-resident persons receiving Canadian rental income to be taxed on a net basis; (ii) the s. 217 election for non-residents to file a Part I return on certain Canadian-source investment income; (iii) the GST/HST joint election under s. 273 of the Excise Tax Act for closely related corporations to treat intercorporate supplies as otherwise than for consideration; (iv) the election under s. 150 of the Excise Tax Act for nil consideration in exempt or nominal supplies among closely related registrants; (v) the Quick Method of accounting election under ss. 170/171 of the Excise Tax Act for eligible small vendors; (vi) the fiscal-year election under s. 156 of the Excise Tax Act; and (vii) for hybrid mismatch structures, the OECD-compliant hybrid mismatch rules in ss. 18.2 and 18.4 of the Income Tax Act operate to deny disproportionate deductions on hybrid financial instruments, hybrid payee entities, and hybrid transfers involving Canadian entities; a foreign entity may make a s. 216-related election or use the 'treaty-based' non-resident disclosure process to claim treaty relief where applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, commonly referred to at the federal level as GST
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies from commercial activity (the 'small supplier' threshold) for both residents and non-residents; registration becomes mandatory once the threshold is exceeded, with liability applying to the supply that caused the excess. A non-resident that solicits orders or advertises in Canada is deemed to carry on business in Canada, and the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies; however, a non-resident that does not otherwise carry on business in Canada may still register voluntarily to recover ITCs on Canadian imports and expenses. Zero-rated exports are excluded from the threshold calculation for the small supplier test. Provincial HST participating provinces (Ontario 13%, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island 15%) require a harmonized rate that includes the 5% federal component and a provincial component, with the Canada Revenue Agency collecting both components; British Columbia imposes separate 5% GST and 7% PST, and Quebec administers its own QST alongside federal GST. For a reverse-logistics enterprise, the place-of-supply rules in ss. 13-17 of the New Harmonized Value-added Tax System Regulations determine whether the supply is made in Canada and therefore subject to 5% GST/HST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate, or government digital stamping; electronic invoicing is voluntary, and the CRA permits the issuance of electronic invoices under s. 263.1 of the Excise Tax Act where the recipient has consented and the invoice is accessible for audit. The Government of Canada has adopted the PEPPOL e-invoicing standard for B2G procurement, requiring suppliers to send invoices electronically to federal departments via the PEPPOL network as a condition of payment for new contracts. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically (GST/HST NETFILE or CRA My Business Account) by registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million, and remittances above that threshold must be made by electronic funds transfer unless the CRA has granted a waiver. No cryptographic stamping or real-time transaction reporting applies; however, the CRA actively audits point-of-sale and logistics-management software for electronic suppression of sales, and possession of suppression software attracts penalties under the Excise Tax Act and Criminal Code offenses.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. (i) Goods exported by the supplier (s. 1, Part V) are zero-rated where the supplier delivers the goods to a common carrier at a Canadian address for shipment outside Canada, delivers them outside Canada, or supplies them as ships' stores for international voyages, and the supplier maintains evidence of export within a reasonable time. (ii) Transportation and freight services, including freight brokerage and cargo-management services incidental to international movement, are zero-rated under ss. 1-6 of Part VII where the freight originates or terminates outside Canada; for a reverse-logistics business, services of arranging export-bound return shipments of graded or reconditioned merchandise qualify. (iii) Services supplied to a non-resident person are zero-rated under s. 7 of Part V where the service is performed entirely outside Canada, or, when performed in Canada, the nature of the service is such that it is not for consumption, use, or enjoyment in Canada; the 'in-Canada enjoyment' exception in s. 7(1)(d)(ii) requires careful documentation for quality-grading, testing, and reconditioning services performed on returned merchandise in Canadian warehouses for foreign principals. (iv) Zero-rating will apply to an intermediary's supply of a service of inspecting, grading, or refurbishing returned goods that are destined for immediate export to the non-resident owner, provided the goods are not further processed or consumed in Canada and adequate proof of export exists. Domestic recovery, storage-for-sale, disposal, or resale services within Canada remain subject to 5% GST/HST. CRA does not prescribe a fixed FX repatriation day-count as an absolute statutory mandate; the 180-day benchmark reflects prudent operational substantiation for the 'reasonable time' evidence requirement used by the CRA in audit practice.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) / Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) or the CBSA export report with unique transaction control number for controlled or regulated goods
Commercial invoice and packing list evidencing the returned goods, their value, and the foreign destination
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (through bill issued to a foreign consignee or freight forwarder) showing delivery outside Canada
Proof of export from the freight forwarder or customs broker, including the foreign customs import declaration or destination-country customs clearance certificate
Foreign exchange remittance records (bank SWIFT/MT103, Airwallex payment confirmations) evidencing inbound FX settlement from the non-resident principal
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit advice matching the invoice amount and the export transaction within the CRA's reasonable-evidence window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA applies rigorous export-evidence scrutiny under ss. 169 and 180 of the Excise Tax Act: input tax credits and zero-rated treatment are denied where the registrant fails to produce 'appropriate evidence in such form and containing such information as will enable the amount to be determined'. Insufficient documentary proof triggers additional assessment of unremitted 5% GST/HST, arrears interest at the prescribed rate compounded daily, and the s. 280(1) penalty of 6% of the net tax for a first late return or 10% plus 2% per month for repeat failures. Fraudulent export zero-rating or fictitious reverse-logistics invoices attract: (i) the s. 285.1 false-statement penalty (greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the falsely claimed amounts); (ii) gross-negligence penalties under s. 285(1) of the Excise Tax Act and s. 163.2 of the Income Tax Act of up to CAD 100,000 or 50% of the misstatement benefit; (iii) the s. 297(2) false-refund penalty of 50% of the refund or credit claimed; and (iv) criminal prosecution for tax evasion under ss. 239 and 327 of the Excise Tax Act, with fines up to CAD 200,000 and imprisonment for up to two years on summary conviction or five years on indictment. Retrospective reassessment is permitted for up to four years from the filing date, extended to eight years for carelessness and indefinitely for fraud or misrepresentation, and CRA's GST/HST export-verification and 'credible evidence' audit programs use banking-data triangulation, carrier manifests, and customs export data to claw back improperly claimed zero-rating, including penalties calculated from the date of the original return.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), constituted under the Bank of Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. B-2), acting in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for monetary policy, prudential supervision, and anti-money-laundering surveillance respectively.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full and unrestricted convertibility of the Canadian dollar (CAD) on both current and capital accounts, consistent with the IMF Articles of Agreement Article VIII obligations, with no exchange-control licensing regime, no central bank approval for capital import or export, and no dividend or profit-repatriation restrictions. The only material hurdles are tax-based: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (statutory 25% on dividends and certain payments, reduced by income tax treaties to 5% for qualifying corporate shareholders and to 15% for portfolio investors), source documentation requirements for treaty relief (e.g., NR301 / NR302 forms), and the FINTRAC reporting obligation for international electronic fund transfers (EFTs) of CAD 10,000 or more. Remittance flows require appropriate supporting corporate resolutions and transfer-pricing documentation for intercompany charges, but no administrative permit is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds, export receipts, or inbound settlement monies. Exporters and reverse-logistics operators may hold foreign currency freely in domestic or offshore accounts. The only applicable obligation is statistical: entities engaged in international transactions must file Statistics Canada Balance of Payments surveys (e.g., Form BI-20 for non-resident trade or CDN survey forms) where thresholds are exceeded, and financial institutions must report EFTs above CAD 10,000 to FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for transactional settlement rails, but legally constrained from acting as the primary deposit-taking institution. Cross-border EMIs such as Airwallex and Wise Platform operate in Canada as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA, not as banks under the Bank Act; they may provide multi-currency wallets, cross-border payment initiation, and batch disbursement clearing for a reverse-logistics entity, but are barred from offering regulated deposit products, lien-capable escrow, or lending facilities. Legal constraints include mandatory FINTRAC MSB registration, parallel KYC/UBO verification at the EMI, and the requirement that the sponsoring Canadian bank be informed of any third-party EMI processor to mitigate unauthorized third-party settlement and concentration risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a federal Business Corporation (CA_CORP) in the low-risk ISIC 5229 reverse-logistics segment, the major Canadian banks require at least one authorized signatory—preferably a director or senior officer resident in Canada—to complete an initial in-branch or secure video-based KYC interview. Fully remote account opening is conditionally permitted at RBC, TD, BMO, Scotiabank, and CIBC where the entity holds a valid CBCA Certificate of Incorporation, the ultimate beneficial ownership structure is transparent and simple, and the signatory passes biometric identity verification against Canadian credit-bureau and sanctions-screening databases plus a notarized corporate resolution. If no presenter has Canadian physical presence, the banks will mandate an in-person branch interview at a designated commercial banking center or a physical attestation before a Canadian notary public or embassy consular officer of the full onboarding package (certificate of incorporation, by-laws, initial directors' resolution, UBO register, and signature authorities).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or remote ultimate beneficial owners with no verifiable Canadian footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies, 90-day proof of residential address, professional reference letters from a regulated financial institution, a complete ownership-chain chart from the ultimate parent to CA_CORP, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations, audited financial statements of the parent for the last two fiscal years, CBCA Certificate of Incorporation, share register, and register of directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector misclassification of the entity as a freight forwarder, customs broker, or high-risk logistics intermediary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal corporate-purpose narrative quoting ISIC 5229 / NAICS 488510 (returned-merchandise reverse logistics and quality grading), executed service agreements with e-commerce principals, warehouse operating leases or subleases proving physical facility control, an organizational chart demonstrating no transportation-carrier authority, and confirmation that no customs-bonded or money-service licensing is triggered.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction volumes and wire frequencies inconsistent with the KYC revenue profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved 12-month cash-flow forecast, unit-economics model for reverse-logistics processing fees, sample invoices and merchant settlement statements, a structured memorandum of the refund and disbursement process, and expected weekly wire volumes under the target rails (Local ACH and Airwallex).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursements to high-risk or sanction-adjacent jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A vetted whitelist of counterparty banks and merchants, sanctions-screening results, end-beneficiary declarations for each disbursement stream, documented commercial rationale for any non-OECD suppliers, and periodic FINTRAC EFT reporting logs demonstrating the absence of prohibited transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dependence on a third-party EMI (Airwallex) without a principal Canadian bank relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of the EMI's FINTRAC MSB registration and tier-1 correspondent-banking arrangement, a downstream KYC delegation agreement with the EMI, contractual confirmation that client settlement funds are held in segregated omnibus accounts, and the Canadian principal bank's signed acknowledgment of the third-party processor arrangement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound equity or intercompany debt injections must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the ultimate parent's bank to a designated Capital Escrow Account at a Canadian tier-1 bank (RBC or CIBC). The remittance information in field 70 must reference the CBCA federal corporation number, the legal account name 'CA_CORP', and the nature of payment in one of two approved forms: 'Equity capital contribution' (Statistics Canada BOP direct-investment code EQL) or 'Shareholder loan - intra-group finance' (BOP code IDL). The receiving bank will verify the underlying corporate resolution, the subscribed-share certificate ledger, and the source-of-funds statement of the parent; for intercompany debt, an executed loan agreement with arm's-length interest-rate terms must be presented to support Part XIII withholding-tax exemption or treaty reduction. The injection may be executed in CAD or USD; where USD is received, conversion is conducted at the bank's wholesale dealing desk or by a pre-agreed spot contract with no Canadian exchange-control approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements under the reverse-logistics model should use three principal clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 COVER through a Canadian correspondent) for cross-border vendor and consumer-refund payments above CAD 10,000 or directed outside North America, with USD wires cleared via CHIPS or Fedwire by the Canadian bank's US correspondent; (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (sight or usance, issued under UCP 600 and routed via SWIFT MT700) where supplier credit enhancement or inventory pre-financing is required; and (c) Payment Canada's Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) and Lynx real-time gross settlement system for domestic CAD refunds and sub-CAD-10,000 ACH transactions, supplemented by card-network rails for consumer-initiated refunds via the original tender card. The identified target rails—Local ACH and Airwallex—remain operationally compatible: Airwallex executes international wires through its tier-1 partner banks while the Canadian operational account maintains Lynx/ACSS connectivity for domestic clearing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable over-the-counter FX forwards (spot-plus-forward) in CAD/USD and CAD/EUR under an ISDA master agreement or short-form FX confirmation, requiring no Canadian exchange-control authorization
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing restricted or low-liquidity emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, IDR, VND) synthetically converted against CAD and cash-settled in USD

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for matched intercompany funding between the foreign parent and CA_CORP, exchanging principal and fixed-rate interest in CAD against USD or EUR, with valuation aligned to transfer-pricing policy and hedge-accounting criteria under IFRS 9
Plain-vanilla European-style FX options under the ISDA 1998 FX and Currency Option Definitions, employed where a cash-flow hedge with zero-premium optionality is operationally justified

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Annual Return (s.263) with ISC information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation or of the corporation's continuation into Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 200; failure to file for two consecutive years authorizes the Director to administratively dissolve the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end of the corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month (max 12 months); additional fines and potential criminal sanctions for gross negligence or willful default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A CBCA distributing corporation must appoint an independent auditor. A non-distributing (private) corporation may waive the statutory auditor appointment annually by unanimous shareholder resolution; no revenue/asset threshold is set by the CBCA for waiver eligibility.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for private corporations, with IFRS optional unless a regulation requires otherwise.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The CBCA mandates an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register; any transfer of shares or change in significant control must be recorded within 15 days of knowledge. The annual return filed with Corporations Canada must confirm current ISC particulars for all controlling shareholders.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Minutes of Shareholders and Directors Meetings (Minute Book)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 255 - 585 per annum (CAD 350 - 800 typical market range)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 12,000 for a private corporation audit; review engagements USD 1,500 - 5,000
